name: Phthalocyanine Blue Pigments
scope: Global phthalocyanine (Pc) blue/green pigment demand outlook to 2035 and which Indian listed pigment makers are positioned for the higher-value electronics/optical grades versus traditional ink, coating and plastics end-uses.

summary.one_line: IndexBox sees Pc blue demand growing ~5% a year to 2035 with electronics/optical grades (PB 15:6, stabilised PB 15:4) the fastest-growing slice, but none of the Indian listed makers we reviewed has disclosed electronics-grade products or capex. Their exposure today is to commodity ink/coating/plastics grades, where overcapacity is the near-term story.
key_points: IndexBox forecasts global Pc blue pigment consumption to grow at a 5.0% CAGR over 2026-2035, taking its market index to 163 in 2035 (2025=100); it sees the electronics/optical segment rising from 15-18% of demand in 2026 to 22-25% by 2035 (S1).

IndexBox says specialty grades (PB 15:6, stabilised PB 15:4) command a 30-50% price premium over commodity grades, and that raw materials (copper, phthalic anhydride, energy) make up 55-65% of production cost (S1).

Colour-filter use is technically distinct: epsilon-form PB 15:6 is preferred for LCD colour filters because its maximum transmission sits at the shortest wavelength, and high pigment purity is a prerequisite for stable pastes and photoresists (S17). DIC sells PB 15:6-based FASTOGEN BLUE colour-filter grades with sub-micron particle-size control (S16).

Meghmani Organics says it is among the top 3 global Pc pigment players with ~14% global share (S2). But its pigment plants ran at only 39% utilisation in Q1 FY27, with production down 14% YoY to 3,233 MT, and management blamed demand pressure and industry overcapacity (S4, S5).

Sudarshan Chemical became a global-scale pigment company after completing the Heubach acquisition on 3 March 2025 (S8, S7). Its Q1 FY27 pigment revenue was Rs 2,605 crore, and management says it needs no new volume capex to hit its FY27 guidance (S6).

Asahi Songwon is a focused CPC-blue player with 13,800 MTPA of blue capacity (CPC crude, Beta and Alpha Blue). Utilisation recovered to 85-90% after restocking, and customers include DIC, Sun Chemical, Clariant and BASF (S11).

In the sources we reviewed, none of the Indian listed makers (Meghmani, Sudarshan, Asahi Songwon, AksharChem, Vipul, Ushanti) discloses a colour-filter or electronics-grade Pc product line or capex. On current evidence, the electronics-grade opportunity for Indian listed names is aspirational, not revenue (S4, S6, S11, S12).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Scale incumbents in commodity Pc blue gain from any volume recovery. Asahi Songwon's blue-pigment utilisation rose from ~60% in FY24 to 85-90% as customers restocked (S11), and its Q1 FY27 consolidated net profit was Rs 19.2 crore vs Rs 3.2 crore a year earlier (S13).

Sudarshan's global portfolio, with ~1,600 products and 19 sites in 11 countries (S6), gives it the broadest access among Indian names to specialty end-uses. Management cited growth in regulated specialty packaging and digital inks (S6).
Meghmani's pigment EBITDA margin improved to 12.1% in Q1 FY27 on better realisations and cost cuts, even at 39% utilisation (S4, S5).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Overcapacity: Meghmani expects pigment utilisation to stay around current levels (S5). IndexBox puts 70-80% of Pc production capacity in China, with 15+ significant Chinese makers (S1).

Raw-material swings: Asahi Songwon's inputs are mostly crude-derived, and CARE notes a lag between raw-material price changes and product price resets (S11). AksharChem's CPC-green line depends on CPC blue crude and aluminium chloride (S12).
Customer concentration: Asahi Songwon's key clients (DIC, Sun Chemical, Clariant, BASF) were ~50% of revenue in H1 FY25, down from 70-80% earlier (S11).
Trade exposure: AksharChem's 9M FY26 margins were hit by the 50% US tariff on Indian exports, and CARE revised its outlook to Negative (S12).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Meghmani pigment utilisation, currently 39%, and whether realisation gains hold (S4, S5).
Sudarshan's One SAP go-live in FY27 and delivery on FY27 guidance of Rs 9,800-10,200 crore revenue and Rs 800 crore EBITDA (S6).
Any disclosure by an Indian listed maker of PB 15:6, colour-filter or electronics-grade qualification. None was found this edition.
Trade remedies on inputs such as the recommended extension of anti-dumping duty on phthalic anhydride from China and Korea (S23), and China's anti-dumping duty on Indian phthalocyanine (S22).

subsections.title: What Pc pigment is and how it is made

blocks.text: Copper phthalocyanine (CuPc) is a synthetic blue pigment and has historically been the highest-volume pigment produced globally. It is made commercially either by heating phthalonitrile with copper(I) chloride at 200-240°C or by the phthalic anhydride/urea route, which can reach yields above 95% (S18). It crystallises in several polymorphs, with the alpha and beta forms the most common (S18). The crude product (CPC blue crude) is the upstream input for Alpha Blue and Beta Blue pigments. Chlorinated with aluminium chloride, it yields Pigment Green 7 (S11, S12).

blocks.caption: Pc pigment grades and where they go
rows: High-purity electronics/optical grades, e.g. LCD colour filters

blocks.text: Patent literature says epsilon-form PB 15:6 is preferred for LCD colour filters because its maximum transmission wavelength is the shortest of the CuPc forms. It also says high pigment purity is a prerequisite for a stable paste or pigmented photoresist (S17). DIC's colour-filter blues (FASTOGEN BLUE, PB 15:6-based) are sold in standard, high-contrast and high-brightness grades. They require sub-micron particle-size control, high transmittance and resistance to agglomeration during photolithography (S16). IndexBox says such specialty grades carry a 30-50% price premium over commodity variants (S1).

Making a different crystal form alone does not make a product electronics-grade. Suppliers also need dispersion and surface-treatment know-how and qualification with photoresist and display-panel customers, and the incumbent suppliers, such as DIC, are Japanese/European majors (S16).

IndexBox (28 Sep 2026) forecasts 5.0% CAGR in global Pc blue consumption over 2026-2035, taking its index to 163 by 2035 (2025=100). It sees electronics/optical rising from 15-18% of demand in 2026 to 22-25% in 2035, driven by display colour filters, conductive inks and functional coatings (S1). Its current segment table puts printing inks at 35%, paints and coatings at 30%, plastics at 20% and electronics/optical at 10%. That 10% does not match its own 15-18% figure for 2026, so treat the segment baseline as approximate (S1).

blocks.title: IndexBox: electronics/optical share of Pc blue demand (range midpoint)
blocks.source: Source: IndexBox (S1); midpoints of 15-18% and 22-25% ranges computed by us

sections.title: Industry structure, trade policy and capex

blocks.text: IndexBox places Asia-Pacific at 55% of demand and says China holds 70-80% of production capacity. Its top-five producer list includes two Indian companies, Sudarshan Chemical and Meghmani Organics, alongside BASF, Clariant and DIC/Sun Chemical (S1). Some of those European assets are now Indian-owned: Clariant sold its pigments business to Heubach/SK Capital in 2022, and Sudarshan acquired Heubach, completing the deal in March 2025 (S9, S8). Meghmani says it holds ~14% of global Pc pigment share and ranks among the top 3 by capacity (S2). Indian makers are export-oriented: exports were ~56% of Asahi Songwon's standalone income in FY24 (S11) and ~55% of AksharChem's sales in 9M FY26 (S12).

items: Global Trade Alert records a Chinese definitive anti-dumping duty on imports of phthalocyanine from India (S22).

India has moved to extend anti-dumping duty on phthalic anhydride, a key Pc input: the recommended duty is $40.08/t on Chinese imports and $140.17/t on Korean imports (S23). This protects domestic PA producers but raises input costs for pigment makers.

Capex is modest. Sudarshan says it needs no new volume capex to reach its growth targets and is evaluating only ROI-led backward integration (S6). Asahi Songwon had no major capex commitments in the near term as of CARE's January 2025 rating (S11). AksharChem's recent capex went into precipitated silica, not pigments (S12).
Meghmani is running pigments at 39% utilisation (S4), so it has spare capacity and no stated need for new pigment lines.

blocks.text: We found no announced Indian listed-company capex for PB 15:6 or colour-filter-grade Pc pigment in any source reviewed this edition.

blocks.text: Our reading of the evidence is that Indian listed makers participate in the growing Pc market mainly through the traditional ink, coatings and plastics base. Asahi Songwon and AksharChem are backward-linked through CPC crude and green respectively (S11, S12). Meghmani is large in commodity blue and green (S2). Sudarshan is the only one with a global specialty portfolio that could plausibly reach higher-spec applications, but it has not disclosed colour-filter products (S6).

items: Sudarshan Colorants India (formerly Heubach Colorants India / Clariant Chemicals India), renamed on 12 Dec 2025 (S10). It sells organic and inorganic high-performance pigments and pigment preparations. Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 222.39 crore and net profit Rs 20.36 crore (S10).
DIC India is a listed Indian printing-ink maker (S24) and a Pc pigment consumer. Its Japanese parent sells PB 15:6 colour-filter pigments (S16), but that business is not in the Indian listed entity.

blocks.text: Market-cap coverage: Sudarshan is the largest name at ~Rs 9,551 crore (S20). There is no large-cap pure Pc pigment maker listed in India. Most of the universe is small or micro cap: Meghmani ~Rs 1,489 crore (S19), Asahi Songwon ~Rs 456 crore (S21).

sections.title: Coverage and what is priced in

items: CARE upgraded Asahi Songwon to CARE A with a Positive outlook in January 2025, citing improved realisations, inventory restocking and consolidation in the pigment industry (S11).
CARE reaffirmed AksharChem at CARE A- but revised its outlook to Negative in February 2026, citing weak dye-intermediate/pigment realisations and US tariffs (S12).

Media coverage of Meghmani's Q1 FY27 focused on margin recovery despite a 14% fall in pigment production and 39% utilisation (S5). Coverage of Sudarshan's Q1 FY27 focused on integration gains, with Heubach-acquired business EBITDA margin at 6.5% vs 15.3% for legacy Sudarshan (S6).
We found no broker or media coverage linking any of these stocks to electronics-grade Pc demand. The IndexBox electronics theme does not appear to be part of the stock narratives yet.

blocks.title: Share-price returns to late Sep 2026
blocks.source: Source: Value Research (S19), Kotak Neo (S20, S21)

blocks.text: All three stocks rallied sharply over six months as margins recovered. Asahi Songwon nearly doubled (S21) and Sudarshan rose ~57% (S20). On a one-year view, however, Meghmani is still down ~31% (S19) and Sudarshan ~11% (S20). The rally reflects a cyclical margin recovery in commodity pigments, not an electronics-grade re-rating.

items: Input costs: raw materials are 55-65% of Pc production cost (S1). Asahi Songwon's inputs are mostly crude-oil derivatives, and it absorbed inventory losses in FY23-FY24 (S11).

Chinese competition: China holds 70-80% of production capacity (S1). CARE linked Asahi's FY24 margin squeeze partly to excess domestic supply after anti-dumping duty was imposed on pigments by China (S11).
Customer concentration: ~50% of Asahi Songwon's H1 FY25 revenue came from key global colorant majors (S11).
Integration and execution: Sudarshan's One SAP go-live is pending in FY27. RIECO, Sudarshan's engineering subsidiary outside pigments, posted negative EBITDA in Q1 FY27 (S6).
The electronics-grade opportunity is aspirational: there is no disclosed PB 15:6 revenue at Indian listed makers, and incumbents such as DIC already sell dedicated colour-filter grades (S16).
Q2 FY27 results (Oct-Nov 2026): Meghmani pigment utilisation against the current 39% (S4), and Sudarshan's progress toward FY27 EBITDA guidance of Rs 800 crore (S6).

Any Indian listed-company announcement of PB 15:6, stabilised PB 15:4 or colour-filter customer qualification. This would be the first hard evidence of participation in the segment IndexBox expects to grow fastest (S1).
The final outcome on the phthalic anhydride anti-dumping extension (S23).

companies.name: Meghmani Organics Ltd
companies.role: Among top-3 global Pc pigment players with ~14% global share (company claim) (S2). Pigments were ~25% of Q1 FY27 revenue (S4).
companies.impact: Exposed to the traditional ink/coating/plastics base, with no disclosed electronics-grade move. Utilisation is at 39% and management expects it to stay around current levels due to overcapacity (S4, S5).

companies.name: Sudarshan Chemical Industries Ltd
companies.role: Global pigment major after acquiring Heubach in March 2025 (S8). IndexBox lists it among the top-5 Pc blue producers (S1).
companies.impact: Broadest specialty reach among Indian names, citing growth in regulated packaging and digital inks. Q1 FY27 pigment revenue was Rs 2,605 crore and it needs no volume capex (S6); no colour-filter disclosure.

companies.name: Asahi Songwon Colors Ltd
companies.role: Focused CPC blue crude, Beta Blue and Alpha Blue maker with 13,800 MTPA of capacity, supplying DIC, Sun Chemical, Clariant and BASF (S11).
companies.impact: Direct beneficiary of commodity blue volume recovery. Utilisation rose to 85-90% (S11) and Q1 FY27 PAT was Rs 19.2 crore (S13). Offset printing ink is its main end-use, and no electronics grade is disclosed (S11).

companies.name: AksharChem (India) Ltd
companies.role: Makes CPC green (Pigment Green 7) with 2,400 MTPA of capacity and REACH registration for up to 1,000 MTPA of EU exports (S12).
companies.impact: Commodity green exposure. 9M FY26 swung to a Rs 5.24 crore loss on weak realisations and US tariffs, and CARE's outlook is Negative (S12).

companies.name: Ushanti Colour Chem Ltd
companies.role: NSE SME-listed maker of copper phthalocyanine, blue crude and Pc pigments at Vatva, with 2,820 MT installed capacity (S14).
companies.impact: Micro-cap exposure to traditional textile/ink/paint end-uses (S14); no electronics-grade disclosure.

companies.name: Vipul Organics Ltd
companies.role: BSE-listed organic pigment maker selling SunTone Pigment Blue 15.0/15.3 copper phthalocyanine grades (S15).
companies.impact: Small participant in standard coatings-grade Pc blue (S15); no electronics-grade disclosure.

companies.name: Sudarshan Colorants India Ltd
companies.role: Formerly Clariant Chemicals India and then Heubach Colorants India (S9); now part of the Sudarshan group. Sells high-performance pigments and pigment preparations (S10).
companies.impact: Adjacent specialty-pigment exposure through the Sudarshan group. Q1 FY27 net profit rose 19% to Rs 20.36 crore (S10).

companies.name: DIC India Ltd
companies.role: Listed Indian printing-ink maker (S24) and a downstream consumer of Pc pigments.
companies.impact: Benefits from ink demand, not Pc manufacturing. Its parent DIC Corp sells PB 15:6 colour-filter pigments (S16), but that business is outside the Indian listed entity.

method: First edition, researched on 2026-09-29 with web search and direct page fetches. Primary inputs were the IndexBox market note (S1), CARE credit-rating rationales for Asahi Songwon and AksharChem (read in full from the PDFs), and company and news coverage of Q1 FY27 results. Company pages and filings that blocked fetching (Meghmani site, BSE/NSE PDFs) are cited only for what was visible in search results. Dates marked 2026-09-29 are access dates where no publication date was shown. Share-price data come from Value Research and Kotak Neo pages dated 25-29 Sep 2026; the dashboard's screener numbers take precedence. The IndexBox segment table has an internal inconsistency (10% vs 15-18% electronics share), which is flagged in the report. Other Indian dye companies (Bodal, Kiri, Jagson) were checked and excluded because no source confirmed Pc pigment manufacture. We found no evidence of electronics-grade Pc output at any Indian listed company. No ratings or price targets are given.
